item.description:
What do the experts at the Nicholas Institute for Energy, Environment & Sustainability actually do? Why do they do it? Who benefits? Find out at Grounds for Conversation, a new monthly coffee hour open to all Duke students.
The second installment in our series on Wednesday, October 21, will feature Kyle Bradbury (see full bio), faculty fellow at the Nicholas Institute, faculty in the Master of Interdisciplinary Data Science program, and assistant research professor with the Pratt School of Engineering and Nicholas School of the Environment.

Insights about research projects, policy engagement, and career paths Answers to your questions about the Nicholas Institute's work Your morning coffee or tea

item.title: DMI/MEMS Seminar Presented by Prof Bradley D Olsen — Wed Oct 21, 12:00 PM — Fitzpatrick Center Schiciano Auditorium Side A
item.description:
Abstract: The exponential rise in the production and use of polymers, particularly in single use applications, has led to a dramatic increase in their environmental prevalence and problems with plastic waste management. One necessary component of the solution to this challenge is developing plastics that degrade more effectively in the environment, be it due to accidental release, composting, or presence in sewage. While this need has been widely known for decades, slow innovation cycles, inertia in our materials systems, and cost and performance barriers have dramatically limited the number of new materials that come to market.
This talk will present a vision for workflows of the future that can be used to accelerate materials innovation through a combination of high-throughput measurement, data science, and machine learning and will apply these workflows to facilitate the discovery of new materials that improve sustainability. item.title: Switch Theatre Company Presents August Wilson's Radio Golf — Thu Oct 22, 7:00 PM — Durham Arts Council
item.description:
Harmond Wilks is on the verge of becoming Pittsburgh’s first Black mayor, and his ambitious redevelopment project for the Hill District – including a new golf course – promises economic growth and a new future. But his plans may be derailed by a single rundown house owned by long time resident “Old Joe” Barlow, who may have a deeper connection to Harmond’s past. Along with his upwardly-mobile business partner Roosevelt, his public relations mastermind wife Mame, and street-smart handyman Sterling, Harmond is forced to confront the cost of progress, the meaning of legacy, and the value of community. The riveting final chapter of August Wilson’s 10-play American Century Cycle, Radio Golf is a compelling and timely drama that challenges us to consider what we are willing to sacrifice for the sake of the future.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Beyond the SDGs: What Did We Learn, and What Comes Next? — Tue Oct 20, 12:00 PM — Trent Drive Hall 040
item.description:
In 2015, United Nations member states adopted the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a Blueprint for achieving a set of interconnected targets to advance global health, equity and development. With just four years left before the SDGs' 2030 end date, it's clear many of these milestones won't be met. What, then, was the value of adopting the SDGs, and what should come next?
With lessons from the SDGs as a guide, this Think Global panel will ask whether the world should adopt a new set of goals to succeed the SDGs after their 2030 expiration, and if so, what those goals should prioritize. Panelists will tackle these questions drawing on their diverse disciplines and expertise-political economy, public policy, family medicine, demography, disease modeling, financing and health economics.

item.title: Women, Youth, and Anti-Colonial Struggle in South Africa’s Exiled Liberation Movements — Tue Oct 20, 12:00 PM — Smith Warehouse
item.description: Using the archives of the African National Congress of South Africa & the letters and memoirs of past activists, this talk will examine how women shaped the exiled struggle against apartheid in South Africa. From the 1960s through the 1980s, South African women pushed the mainstream of the anti-apartheid movement to consider women's particular suffering under apartheid, and to fight for broad social transformation as part of overthrowing apartheid. At the same time, within the movement, generational tensions also sparked conversation and at times heated disagreement over topics like sex education, access to birth control, and the right to family life within a militarized revolutionary movement. These challenging conversations reveal that younger generations of exiles brought new political ideas into the movement from the mid-1970s onwards, transforming an aging political organization into a more militant formation. item.title: Vintage Rides Ride — Sun Oct 25, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Carolina Tarwheels Cycling Club What is a Vintage Rides Ride? Well, it's where we pull out the old bikes and remember (or imagine) what it was like in the old days, when bikes were (mostly) steel, tires were skinny, jerseys were wool, and pedals had toe clips ("toe cages" to you younger folks). Shifters were generally on the down tube, and friction operated- no one had to charge any batteries before the ride. So bring your classics, or ride anything at all, but come along for a relaxed, easy ride. All riders and all bikes are welcome! Route here: [https://ridewithgps.com/routes/39713600](https://ridewithgps.com/routes/39713600) or something similar. **Route subject to change at the leader's whim** (often based on what kind of gearing we're on). Distance approximately 20 miles. We will regroup if necessary, so no one will be left out there.
It is Tarwheels policy for all riders to sign the ride waiver before coming out to the ride.
